data.name: Kutub
data.gender_notes: Kutub is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Kutub refers to the sacred scriptures and teachings of Islam. The term comes from the Arabic word kutubah, meaning a book or scroll. Kutub are considered the foundation of Islamic law and practice, and include the Quran, Hadith, and Sunnah. The name Kutub carries the meaning “Repository of Knowledge” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kutub usually hope their child will grow to embody repository of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of knowledge and wisdom, rooted in the Islamic faith.
data.etymology: Kutub belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Repository of Knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kutub total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The term Kutub holds great cultural significance in the Islamic world, representing the collective body of sacred texts and teachings that form the foundation of the Islamic faith. The importance of the Kutub is reflected in the way they are preserved, transmitted, and studied. Over the centuries, scholars have dedicated their lives to preserving, translating, and interpreting the Kutub, ensuring their accuracy and accessibility to future generations. Many Muslim communities have established special libraries, known as Kutubkhana, to house and protect these sacred texts.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the Kutub are considered the source of guidance and inspiration for Muslims, offering a roadmap for leading a virtuous and God-conscious life. The Quran, the maqam mahmud or the Praised Station, is the most revered of the Kutub, serving as the literal word of God revealed to Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). The Hadith and Sunnah, which provide the practical examples and interpretations of the Quranic teachings, are also essential aspects of the Kutub. Through the study and application of the Kutub, Muslims seek to deepen their connection with God, gain a better understanding of the divine commandments, and cultivate virtues such as compassion, patience, and humility.
